cards.text: Joseph, Jacob's son, has settled his father's whole family in Egypt, as Pharaoh, king of Egypt, commanded, and he's providing them with food (Genesis 47:11-12). But in all that region, there's no food. The famine is so severe that Egypt and Canaan are worn all the way out.
So people buy grain from Joseph, and he collects ALL the money to be found in Egypt and Canaan. Friend, Mother Miller bought me for ONE quarter, and I still thought somebody had splurged.

cards.question: Joseph now has the money of Egypt and Canaan. Where does he bring it all?
Then the money in Egypt and Canaan runs out. The Egyptians come to Joseph and ask him for food. True or false?

cards.text: And they don't hold back. They tell him, "Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? For our funds have run out!"

cards.question: With the Egyptians' money gone, Joseph gives them food for free. True or false?

cards.text: Joseph tells them to bring him their livestock instead, and all through that year he gives them food for their horses, flocks, herds and donkeys. Somewhere in that line, I just KNOW there's a man handing over a donkey's rope and asking if he gets a receipt.

cards.question: That year ends. In the second year, the Egyptians come back to Joseph with their money and their livestock gone. What do they say is all they have left?
So the Egyptians ask Joseph to buy them and their land in exchange for food. What do they say they will become?
Along with food, the Egyptians ask Joseph for seed, so they can live and the land won't become desolate. True or false?

cards.text: And the deal goes through. One and all, the Egyptians sell their fields, because the famine is so severe upon them, and the land becomes Pharaoh's.
Joseph reduces the people to servitude from one end of Egypt to the other. But there's one group whose land Joseph doesn't acquire.

cards.question: The one group in Egypt whose land Joseph doesn't acquire is the ___.
The priests don't sell their land, because they eat the rations Pharaoh supplies them. True or false?

cards.text: Then Joseph tells the people, "Now that I have acquired you and your land for Pharaoh this day, here is seed for you to sow in the land." SEED in a famine, friend, that's like finding fresh dough right after you scraped the last crumbs off the tray!

cards.question: Here's Joseph's deal: at harvest, a fifth goes to Pharaoh. What happens to the other four-fifths?
What do the people tell Joseph when they hear his terms?
Joseph's law that a fifth of the produce goes to Pharaoh only lasts until the famine ends. True or false?

cards.text: We'll leave Egypt right there for now. Stick around, friend, because this family's story is still in the oven.
